description: Rust toolchain for any Rust repository: `channel` in rust-toolchain.toml and every `rust` Docker image tag move in one pull request that cannot ship half-done. Never touches `rust-version` in Cargo.toml; applications that want it moved too extend rust-application instead.

packageRules.description: The Rust toolchain moves in one pull request: `channel` in rust-toolchain.toml (depName `rust`, rust-toolchain manager) and the `rust:<version>` Docker images (depName `rust`, docker datasource) name the same release and must not drift apart. Digest updates (same release, rebuilt image) stay ungrouped. Repositories with more members, such as a cargo-chef image tagged with the Rust version, add a rule with the same groupName.

Keeps the `rust toolchain` group whole while a member is inside `minimumReleaseAge`. Under the default `internalChecksFilter: strict`, Renovate drops pending updates from a branch that also holds ready ones, so a toolchain bump can ship without its base image. `none` keeps every update in the branch and reports the pending age as the `renovate/stability-days` status; `platformAutomerge: false` hands the merge to Renovate, which waits for that status, where GitHub's native auto-merge only waits for required checks. Matched without `matchUpdateTypes`: Renovate reads `internalChecksFilter` before an update type exists, so a rule narrowed by update type never applies it.

Docker Hub stamps a tag with its last push, and the official `rust` images are rebuilt on every base image update, so `rust:<version>` keeps looking days old or less long after the release. The toolchain member (rust-version datasource, real release dates) carries the release age for the whole group; on the image it would only keep the group pending. Digest updates keep the age gate, because there the push is the change.
